importance_ranking.reason: Greenhouse type (Quonset tunnel vs multi-span vs sawtooth vs fan-and-pad) is visually distinct and immediately communicates scale, technology tier, and suitability for the buyer's crop and land. A buyer scanning listings uses the image to eliminate wrong structure types before reading any text — wrong type means immediate skip.

Greenhouse Type, Covering Material, and Ventilation Type are primary shortlisting criteria — they determine NHB/MIDH subsidy eligibility, crop suitability, and climate control capability. Buyers cannot evaluate fit without these specs; listings missing them cannot be shortlisted.

Per-sq-meter cost varies dramatically across structure types (naturally ventilated vs fan-and-pad vs polycarbonate) and is the primary budget planning input for subsidy-linked procurement. Indian agri-buyers are highly price-sensitive and use listed per-sq-m rates to shortlist contractors before engaging — price is a discovery signal, not just a confirmation signal.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Small terrace/home greenhouse kits may be quoted per unit or per set; greenhouse components (GI pipes, film rolls) quoted per piece or per running meter. Per sq meter is the dominant commercial unit aligned with NHB/MIDH subsidy norms and must be shown to enable price comparison.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listings without unit clarity — some sellers quote per sq ft, per sq meter, or per unit (for kit products), creating real confusion. NHB/MIDH subsidy norms denominate in per sq meter, making unit display essential for the primary commercial buyer segment.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand with buyer recall exists in the Indian greenhouse market — the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and contractors; buyers search by structure type and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: For large commercial and subsidy-linked projects, buyers evaluate contractor track record, installation experience, and post-sale support during vendor selection — company matters but only after spec and price shortlisting. No brand commands the kind of recall that would make it a primary search signal.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the fundamental product class (naturally ventilated vs fan-and-pad vs shade house vs glass house) — values are non-interchangeable across crop requirements and subsidy tiers, and drive the largest price delta in the category.

Covering material (poly film vs polycarbonate vs glass vs shade net) determines durability, light transmission, thermal performance, and cost tier — a primary differentiator within the same greenhouse type that significantly changes price and crop suitability.

missing_important_specs.why_important: NHB/MIDH subsidy norms mandate minimum 200-micron UV-stabilised polyethylene film — buyers and subsidy inspectors verify this spec, and it is a primary quality differentiator between compliant and non-compliant structures.

Commercial greenhouse procurement is project-scoped by area (sq meters or acres) — buyers need to know the standard project size or minimum supply area to assess whether the seller can meet their scale requirement.

NHB/MIDH subsidy-linked buyers explicitly filter for structures certified as subsidy-eligible — this is a binary purchase gate for the dominant commercial buyer segment and is absent from the current spec list.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Defines the technology tier and climate control requirement — sellers need this to determine whether they can supply the structure and to price it accurately (naturally ventilated vs hi-tech fan-and-pad vs tunnel are fundamentally different products at different price points).
Project scale determines whether the seller can supply at the required size and directly drives the total project cost estimate — sellers need area to respond with a meaningful quote.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The crop being grown determines ventilation, humidity control, and covering material requirements — sellers need this to recommend the correct structure type and confirm suitability, especially for high-value crops like roses, capsicum, or saffron.
